findings.reason: the section must either name these forks as callers to migrate onto the owner or scope its done-when grep to the primitive's own directory, otherwise the stated gate is unachievable as written and the "the owner holds the generic primitive" claim understates the fork population the plan exists to remove.
findings.text: §8 requires `grep -rn 'os.replace(\|\.replace(path)\|with_suffix(".*\.tmp")' reckon/` to return hits only inside the promoted primitive, but the repository carries sibling-temporary-then-`os.replace` writers the section does not name or migrate: `reckon/ledger.py:1168` (`.{name}.{pid}.tmp` + `os.replace`), `reckon/crew/runs.py:1442` (`.{name}.repair.tmp` + `os.replace`), `reckon/hooks/worker_stop.py:364`, `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:360`, `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:484` — and `reckon/resources.py:1117` renames a staged path into place; the plan inventories only the project-state, checkpoint and `.html.tmp` forks

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §8 promotes one private primitive to one public name that hides temp creation, `O_EXCL`, chmod, file fsync, rename and cleanup behind `(path, render, *, fsync, mode, fsync_directory)`, and explicitly adds no other function to `reckon/project_state.py` or `reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py`, so the surface shrinks while the behaviour stays.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §8 claims to gather "the surviving atomic-writer forks" onto the owner, but its inventory omits at least six sibling-temporary-then-`os.replace` writers, and its own done-when grep cannot hold while they remain.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1474, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §8 states its one added public definition is the promoted primitive and that the retired forks are underscore-private and uncounted, §7 adds no member of any of the four families, and no surface-adding section is silent about what it retires or merges.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design sections cite the mechanisms they extend before adding anything: the code-depth census and the crew pattern review (§1), the existing envelope writer and `reckon._store.write_json_atomically` (§3), and, for the two implementable sections, the named owner `reckon/_store.py:_write_through_sibling_temporary` (:419) plus the forks `reckon/project_state.py:_durable_replace` (:165), `reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py:_replace_atomically` (:242) and the three `.html.tmp` paths in `_store.py` (§8); §7 reads the existing floor site (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:3844`) rather than proposing a new acceptance path.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §8 extends the owner instead of layering over it: it states no new function is added to the forking modules and that each fork becomes a call to the promoted primitive, and it names why the one retained fork (`follow_checkpoint._replace_atomically`) was kept against the document-oriented adapter specifically, not against the render-callback primitive, so the extension is justified rather than a wrapper.
